title: Piaget said children fit a new experience in, or change the schema
summary: OpenStax says Piaget held that children assimilate a new experience into a current schema, or accommodate by changing the schema.
body: OpenStax Psychology says Piaget's children build schemata, mental models for categorizing and interpreting information. Assimilation takes in information that fits what they already know. Accommodation changes a schema when the new information does not fit. The book's example is a child who calls a sheep a dog, then revises the dog schema after being corrected. The pair is his account of how expectations update. It is not an age band.

sources.title: OpenStax Psychology, 9.2 Lifespan Theories
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Psychology web page, CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase; credit OpenStax. Supports the definitions of schemata, assimilation, and accommodation, including the dog-and-sheep example without using the textbook's child name.
